name: Leather goods and tanneries

problems.words: Eid ul Adha skins arrive all at once and we can't process them fast enough
quick_ideas: Write down last Eid's arrivals by day against what you processed, so you see how big the gap was
List the area and collector types who deliver, so next Eid's arrivals can be planned in turns

workzap_build.text: An Eid collection tracker for lots by area and collector type, salting date, arrival and processing queue, visible to the owner each day of the peak.

problems.ask_first: What's the biggest headache in the weeks after Eid ul Adha?
problems.free_stops: How arrivals are scheduled and the queue is managed is set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note this week's unloading times and the time sorting actually starts, so handover delays around skin arrivals become visible.
Give one floor lead the arrivals notebook at one fixed table, so every incoming lot waits in one queue.

problems.words: Collectors grade hides one way, we grade another, always a fight
quick_ideas: Grade the next lot at arrival with the collector present, so the grade is agreed on the spot
Photograph a few hides from each disputed lot, so there is a record

workzap_build.text: A hide intake register for source type, count, weight, grade at receipt and photos, with disputed lots flagged.

problems.ask_first: Do grading fights occur with most collectors, or mainly with one or two?
problems.free_stops: Grade definitions and how disputes are recorded are kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many disputed hides come from each collector type this week, so arguments can be focused where they cost most.
Give one grader the job of marking the agreed grade on arrival, so each lot has one decision point.

problems.words: All our cash goes into hides at Eid and we're stretched for months
quick_ideas: Write down roughly when cash went out at Eid and when it came back from sales, so you see how long it is tied up
List which buyers owe you now, so collection effort goes where it matters

workzap_build.text: A receivables and claims tracker per buyer alongside a view of stock bought and still unsold, kept current every day.

problems.ask_first: Does your cash stay tied up until the leather is sold, or until buyers pay?
problems.free_stops: How the cash picture is built from stock and receivables is detailed in the solution document; for financing, talk to your accountant or bank.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many days each Eid hide lot sits before leaving as finished goods, so the longest lockup point becomes visible.
Give one person one notebook for all buyer dues and promised dates, so chasing happens before the next hide rush.

problems.words: Leather stock in sq ft never matches the books
quick_ideas: Count one grade or colour fully in sq ft and compare with the books, so you see the size of the gap
Keep each lot in a marked place, so lots stop getting mixed

workzap_build.text: Leather stock in sq ft by grade, colour and lot across stores, tracked from raw hide to finished with yield at each stage.

problems.ask_first: Does the mismatch show in one grade or colour, or across all of them?
problems.free_stops: How lots are tracked through each stage is mapped in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare one rack's physical bundles with the book entry this week, so the mismatch is pinned to a place not the whole store.
Give one store person the job of writing every movement in one stock notebook, so returns and issues stop scattering across scraps.

problems.words: Cutting yield is low and karigars waste leather
quick_ideas: For one article, compare leather issued with pieces cut, so you know the real consumption
Collect offcuts from cutting in one place for a week, so you see how much there is

workzap_build.text: A cutting issue and return log per karigar role with expected against actual consumption, and an offcut register.

problems.ask_first: Is yield low on all articles, or mainly on certain ones?
problems.free_stops: How expected consumption is set per article is set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many usable cut pieces come from one hide for one article today, so low yield is tied to a real job.
Give one cutter the job of keeping all offcuts from each article in one marked spot, so waste is linked back to the work.

problems.words: Pieces sent and pieces returned by subcontractors don't match
quick_ideas: Reconcile what each outside karigar has from you today, so you know what is outstanding
Ask for a count confirmation on the next return

workzap_build.text: A subcontractor ledger for pieces sent, received, rejected and paid, flagging shortfalls on the day of return.

problems.ask_first: Is the mismatch with one outside karigar, or with most of them?
problems.free_stops: How counts are confirmed and tied to payment is covered in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare one subcontractor's sent count with the returned count this week, so the exact missing balance is clear before another handover.
Give one dispatch person the job of writing sent and returned pieces in one notebook, so outside work is tracked from one place.

problems.words: Colour or finish varies between lots and the buyer rejects
quick_ideas: Keep an approved swatch for each colour at dispatch, so lots are checked against one standard
Note which lots were rejected and their process dates, so a pattern can be spotted

workzap_build.text: A pre-dispatch check per lot against the approved swatch, with photos and rejection reasons recorded.

problems.ask_first: Does the variation show mostly in colour, or in finish?
problems.free_stops: Check points and how lots are compared are kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Lay rejected lots beside an accepted lot from the same buyer, so the visible difference is agreed before dispatch arguments start.
Give one person the job of keeping one approved piece with each outgoing lot, so checking happens against the same reference.

problems.words: Buyer samples take too long, we lose the order
quick_ideas: List open sample requests with request date and current status, so you see which are stuck
Note what held up the last lost sample, so that step gets attention

workzap_build.text: An order and sample tracker with buyer deadlines and status, alerting when a sample is running late.

problems.ask_first: Are samples slow mostly at making, or while waiting for the buyer's reply?
problems.free_stops: How sample stages are tracked and escalated is set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note the days between sample request and dispatch for each open buyer sample, so the slowest part of the sample routine stands out.
Give one person the job of reviewing all open samples at one fixed time daily, so buyer requests stop waiting between departments.

problems.words: Owner doesn't know which product line actually makes money
quick_ideas: Work out cost per piece for your two main articles using today's hide and chemical rates, so you have a real comparison
Compare it with the selling price of each

workzap_build.text: A costing sheet per article using current hide and chemical rates, with a monthly margin view by product line.

problems.ask_first: Do you sell mostly bags, or a wider mix of leather items?
problems.free_stops: How yield and overheads are built into cost per article is detailed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count pieces started and pieces packed this week for each main product line, so slow moving lines stand out on the floor.
Give one floor lead the job of noting daily started and packed pieces in one notebook, so product line reviews use the same routine each evening.

never_say: Any advice on chemicals, chrome, effluent treatment, environmental permits or how to handle inspectors; gas exposure in pits or drums is an emergency.
Any help calling synthetic "genuine leather", misdeclaring species or origin, or under-invoicing.
Any guidance on animal welfare, halal or religious rulings around qurbani skins.
Any help optimising child labour or unsafe conditions.
Financing advice; suggest an accountant or bank.
Storing names of hide collectors, charities, workers or buyers.

sample_reply.person: Eid ke baad khaalon ka hisaab bilkul bigar jata hai aur collectors se grade pe roz jhagra hota hai. Koi hal hai?
sample_reply.pi:
Haan, is ko behtar kiya ja sakta hai, aur pehla qadam aasan hai.
Pehle, agla lot aamad pe hi collector ke saamne grade kar lein, taa ke grade usi waqt tay ho jaye.
Doosra, pichli Eid ki roz-ba-roz aamad aur processing ka mawazna likh lein, taa ke pata chale gap kitna bara tha.
Workzap is tarah ka intezam kar sakta hai: phone pe hide intake register jahan har lot ki ginti, wazan, grade aur photo aamad pe darj ho, aur Eid ke dino mein har roz processing queue aap ke saamne ho.
